title: Find more counterexamples to multiplicativity (eq. 24); do they support holding for 1 <= p <= 2?

decision.rationale: The two cited constructions supply counterexamples beyond the Werner-Holevo family and settle the 1 < p <= 2 range that the archived statement asks about. Both settling works are cited in the source bibliography only by arXiv identifier (arXiv:0707.0402 and arXiv:0707.3291), and the closing of the p = 2 case is recorded in the narrative as subsequent work by Winter.

formulation.statement:
**Problem 11.** Find additional counterexamples — beyond the Werner–Holevo channel and its small perturbations — to the multiplicativity conjecture
$$
u_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=
u_p(\Phi)\,
u_p(\Omega), 	ag{24}$$
holding for a range of $p>1$. Determine, on the basis of such counterexamples, whether the conjecture is true for $1\le p\le 2$.

question.summary: The source asked for multiplicativity counterexamples beyond the Werner-Holevo channel and its perturbations and whether multiplicativity survives for 1 <= p <= 2. Winter gave counterexamples for every p above 2, Hayden extended them to all 1 < p < 2, and Winter subsequently closed p = 2.
question.importance: Before summer 2007 the Werner-Holevo channel and mildly perturbed variants were the only known counterexamples, several authors had conjectured a safe range 1 <= p <= 2, and the p to 1 limit of the conjecture is the additivity statement Shor showed equivalent to additivity of the Holevo capacity and of the entanglement of formation.

targetClauses.label: Counterexamples to p-norm multiplicativity beyond Werner-Holevo
targetClauses.text: The archived statement asks to find counterexamples to multiplicativity of the maximal output p-norm beyond the Werner-Holevo channel and its small perturbations, holding for a range of p above 1, and to determine on that basis whether the conjecture is true for 1 <= p <= 2.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: New counterexample families covering a range of p above 1, settling in particular whether multiplicativity survives on 1 < p <= 2.

acceptedClaims.title: Winter and Hayden refute multiplicativity for every p above 1
acceptedClaims.text: Winter constructs counterexamples to multiplicativity for every p above 2 using random unitary channels of growing dimension, and Hayden extends the counterexamples to all 1 < p < 2, with Winter subsequently closing the case p = 2. Together they supply the requested counterexamples beyond the Werner-Holevo family and show that multiplicativity fails throughout the conjectured safe range 1 < p <= 2.

cautions.label: Scope
cautions.text: The separate additivity conjecture at p = 1 was refuted later by Hastings (Nature Physics 5, 255 (2009)); that is a distinct statement from p-norm multiplicativity for p > 1.
